scope_note: The Palmer census has been extensively explored previously. This is therefore a newly frozen mechanistic follow-up, not a claim of pristine preregistration. The specific regional-forcing × N_eff interaction defined here has not been computed before this contract.
hypothesis: Loss of within-island breeding-patch diversity increases an island population's coupling to shared regional demographic forcing.
biological_prediction: For the same regional forcing, focal-island annual growth should respond more strongly when effective colony number is low. With N_eff coded so larger values mean more spatially distributed breeding, the regional_forcing × N_eff coefficient is predicted to be negative.

eligibility.reason: These are the three islands with unchanged census colony-code rosters in the frozen Palmer concentration analysis.
eligibility.regional_forcing_rule: For each focal island-year transition, calculate the arithmetic mean annual log1p growth of all available persistent-pool islands after excluding the focal island if it belongs to the pool.
eligibility.focal_transition_rule: Start-year island abundance must be positive and both start and end census years must exist. Litchfield contributes only transitions whose start-year abundance is positive.

variables.effective_colony_number: 1 / sum_j p_ij,t^2, computed from colony-code breeding-pair shares at start year t
variables.regional_forcing: leave-focal-out mean focal-year log1p growth over the persistent regional pool
variables.current_abundance: log1p focal-island breeding-pair abundance at start year t

standardization.effective_colony_number: log1p transform then z-score within focal island over eligible transitions
standardization.current_abundance: z-score within focal island over eligible transitions
standardization.regional_forcing: global z-score over eligible focal-island transitions
standardization.year: global z-score over eligible focal-island transitions

primary_model: focal_growth ~ focal_island_fixed_effects + z_year + z_current_abundance + z_regional_forcing + z_log1p_N_eff + z_regional_forcing:z_log1p_N_eff

inference.null: Within each focal island independently, circularly shift the complete eligible z_log1p_N_eff sequence while leaving focal growth, forcing, abundance, year, island identity and all other variables fixed.
inference.enumeration: Use every non-duplicated combination of island-specific circular shifts, including the identity alignment. No Monte Carlo sampling if the full product is computationally feasible.
inference.p_value: number of null coefficients <= observed coefficient divided by total exact shift combinations
inference.support_rule: Observed interaction must be negative and exact one-sided p <= 0.05.

prespecified_sensitivities.name: persistent-focal-only
prespecified_sensitivities.rule: Repeat the same model and exact circular-shift inference using only COR and HUM, excluding locally extinct LIT.

prespecified_sensitivities.name: count-error-coupling
prespecified_sensitivities.rule: Only if the primary interaction is supported, simulate the already-frozen Poisson, Gamma-Poisson CV10% and Gamma-Poisson CV20% count-error families under time-invariant within-island composition, preserving observed island-total trajectories, and quantify whether shared current-census error can generate an interaction as negative as observed. This sensitivity cannot rescue a failed primary result.

terminal_rules: Do not change focal islands, forcing pool, lag, interaction sign, transform, covariates, or standardization after computing the primary coefficient.
Do not substitute a rolling-window synchrony metric, alternate concentration index, thresholded colony count, or tuned temporal subset if the primary test fails.
Do not claim individual dispersal, prospecting, public-information use, or a causal habitat mechanism from this analysis.
If supported, interpret the result as state-dependent demographic coupling consistent with erosion of a spatial portfolio, not proof of the mechanism generating that state.
